clinicalPearls: Most cases arise from de novo heterozygous loss-of-function variants in CHD7 on chromosome 8, encoding a chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein that remodels chromatin during neural-crest and placodal development.
The acronym captures the classical features: ocular coloboma, heart defects, atresia of the choanae, retardation of growth/development, genital hypoplasia and ear anomalies including deafness.

Updated clinical criteria (Blake and Verloes) emphasise major features of coloboma, choanal atresia, characteristic external ear malformation and hypoplastic semicircular canals rather than requiring all original letters.
The external ear is typically short and wide with a triangular concha, absent lobule and a cup or lop shape, giving a highly recognisable pinna.
Cranial nerve dysfunction is a hallmark: anosmia (I), facial palsy (VII), sensorineural or mixed deafness (VIII) and severe swallowing incoordination (IX/X) causing aspiration.
Absent or hypoplastic semicircular canals on temporal-bone imaging is one of the most sensitive and specific radiological signs and underlies profound balance delay.
Ocular coloboma usually involves the retina and optic disc and may threaten vision, whereas microphthalmia and iris coloboma are less consistent.
Cleft lip/palate, tracheo-oesophageal fistula, hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction with hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism and immune deficiency from thymic hypoplasia broaden the phenotype.
reference.pathophysiology: CHARGE syndrome is an autosomal dominant multisystem disorder caused in the majority of cases by heterozygous pathogenic variants in CHD7, which encodes chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 7, an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeller that regulates transcription of genes governing migration and differentiation of neural-crest cells and cranial placodes during early embryogenesis. Because neural crest and placodal tissue contribute to the eye, cardiac outflow tract, craniofacial skeleton, external and inner ear, olfactory system and multiple cranial nerves, haploinsufficiency of CHD7 produces the characteristic constellation of coloboma, conotruncal and aortic-arch heart defects, choanal atresia, ear malformation with semicircular-canal aplasia and cranial-nerve dysfunction. The gene also influences development of the olfactory bulbs and the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, explaining the frequent combination of anosmia and hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism analogous to Kallmann syndrome, and its role in pharyngeal-pouch derivatives accounts for thymic and parathyroid hypoplasia with resultant immune and calcium disturbance. Most variants are de novo nonsense, frameshift or splice-site mutations, so recurrence risk is usually low, though germline mosaicism and rare familial dominant transmission are described, and there is wide phenotypic variability even within the same variant.
additionalDifferentials: 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge/velocardiofacial) syndrome with conotruncal defects and thymic hypoplasia
Kabuki syndrome with coloboma, ear anomalies and developmental delay
Renal coloboma (PAX2) and other coloboma-associated syndromes
Kallmann syndrome when anosmia and hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism dominate
VACTERL association with overlapping tracheo-oesophageal and cardiac anomalies
Branchio-oto-renal syndrome with ear malformation and deafness
Retinoic-acid embryopathy and other teratogenic causes of coloboma
additionalInvestigations: CHD7 sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis to confirm the molecular diagnosis
High-resolution temporal-bone CT or MRI to demonstrate semicircular-canal aplasia and cochlear anomalies
Comprehensive audiological assessment including brainstem-evoked responses
Dilated ophthalmological examination for coloboma and microphthalmia
Echocardiography for conotruncal and aortic-arch lesions
Endocrine evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and growth
Immunological work-up and lymphocyte subsets for thymic-dependent immune deficiency
redFlags: Bilateral choanal atresia presenting as neonatal respiratory distress relieved by crying and worsened by feeding
Recurrent aspiration and failure to thrive from cranial-nerve IX/X swallowing dysfunction
Cyanotic congenital heart disease requiring urgent cardiological intervention
Profound sensorineural deafness with absent balance function delaying safe mobility
Hypocalcaemia or severe infection suggesting associated parathyroid and thymic hypoplasia
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends chiefly on the severity of cardiac disease, airway compromise and feeding difficulty in infancy, with mortality concentrated in the first years of life; survivors have variable intellectual outcome and most face lifelong sensory impairment, but with multidisciplinary support many achieve meaningful communication and independence.
pitfalls: Expecting all letters of the acronym before making the diagnosis, thereby missing atypical cases defined by ear and semicircular-canal anomalies
Attributing developmental delay solely to intellectual disability when dual sensory loss and balance failure are the main obstacles
Overlooking hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism and delayed puberty because anosmia is not routinely tested
Failing to screen for immune deficiency and hypocalcaemia before surgery or live-vaccine administration
Assuming low recurrence risk without considering parental germline mosaicism
references: Paediatric otolaryngology and audiology reference texts
Consensus diagnostic criteria for CHARGE syndrome
management: Secure the neonatal airway and correct choanal atresia surgically, with tracheostomy where obstruction is severe or recurrent
Address feeding difficulty and aspiration from cranial-nerve dysfunction with speech and language therapy, thickened feeds and nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding as needed
Surgical repair of conotruncal and aortic-arch cardiac defects guided by paediatric cardiology
Early audiological rehabilitation with hearing aids or cochlear implantation for sensorineural or mixed deafness, and ophthalmology management of coloboma with tinted lenses for photophobia
Endocrine hormone replacement for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and growth hormone deficiency where confirmed
Vestibular and developmental physiotherapy to support the profound balance delay of semicircular-canal aplasia
Coordinated multidisciplinary care across ENT, cardiology, audiology, ophthalmology, endocrinology and clinical genetics
Genetic counselling, noting most cases are de novo autosomal dominant CHD7 variants, with parental testing to refine recurrence risk
